chunks: Ahmad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abu Imran al-Armani, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'If you were to share a thousand people in your Hajj, there would be a Hajj for each one, without your Hajj being reduced by anything.'
ai.seo_question: Does sharing others in my Hajj reduce the reward or validity of my own Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility of sharing the reward of Hajj with multiple individuals, emphasizing that the spiritual merit is not divided but multiplied for each participant. It reflects the Shia scholarly view that the act of Hajj is a singular deed whose reward can be extended to others, provided the physical performance remains valid, highlighting the communal nature of Islamic worship.
